chapter: Blackbirds, Carmen Jones and the Ziegfeld Follies
title: No discrimination at the Ziegfeld Theater; respect for Ziegfeld and Gershwin
summary: He says everyone was congenial, there were no special contract clauses, and he admired Ziegfeld and George Gershwin.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Were there any particular clauses in your contract for performing at the Ziegfeld Follies -- you were the only black act, I take it at the Ziegfeld Follies I take it at that time.
Were there any particular clauses in that contract that didn't
I never heard that, never heard that.
Were there any clauses that said anything?
Were you feeling the effects of any kind of discrimination against blacks at this time?
On the stage or off stage, in the audience.
In the Ziegfeld Theater you mean?
Oh, he was great, he was great, God rest his soul. He was great.
Did you know him well? Did you spend much time with him?

Only the time when we signed the contract and go do the show. That's all. George Gershwin was the same way. Great people. Great people, can't do nothing with 'em. When they're great, they're just great, that's all.
There was an enormous respect for him I take it.

Oh, yeah. How can you do otherwise. What would you want to do otherwise? Nothing. To respect a person that has reached a certain pinnacle that you can be proud of and the man took shows, gave people jobs and managed things so, I was proud of him. Same way with George Gershwin.
